title: 고난도 · 비교/변화 (14~15번)
intro: OPIc 14~15번은 과거와 현재 비교, 사회 변화, 찬반 의견처럼 생각을 정리해 말해야 하는 고난도 문제입니다. 20년차 개발자이자 두 아이의 부모라는 페르소나는 이 구간에서 특히 강합니다: 20년 전 신입 때와 지금, 어릴 적 대전과 지금 분당, 금요일 재택근무, 가족 영화의 밤처럼 직접 겪은 변화를 예시로 쓰면 어려운 질문도 쉬운 말로 풀 수 있습니다.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장('Oh, that's a big question. Let me think.') → 입장 또는 변화 한 줄 요약 → 이유·차이 2개 → 내 경험 예시 → 결론 마무리 문장('So yeah, that's what I think.')
비교 문제는 'In the past, ~. But these days, ~.' 와 'The biggest difference is that ~.' 으로 과거와 현재를 분명히 나누세요.
의견 문제는 'I believe that ~ for two reasons.' → First / Second → 'For example, in my case, ~.' → 'All things considered, I think ~.' 순서를 고정합니다.
어려운 단어 대신 쉬운 구어체로 말하고, 신입 때 이야기·아이들 이야기·출퇴근처럼 내 생활 예시를 꼭 하나 넣으세요.

expressions.en: Oh, that's a big question. Let me think.
In the past, ~. But these days, ~.
It has changed a lot over the last 20 years.
I think there are two reasons.
There are good points and bad points.
I work from home on Fridays.
It's much more convenient than before.
Housing prices have gone up so much.
That's why more and more people ~.

expressions.note: 장단점이 함께 있는 변화를 말할 때

expressions.en: I'd say the best option is somewhere in the middle.
expressions.ko: 가장 좋은 건 그 중간쯤이라고 봐요.

expressions.en: So yeah, that's what I think about it.

questions.en: How has housing in Korea changed over the last 20 years? What are the biggest differences between homes today and homes 20 years ago?
questions.ko: 지난 20년간 한국의 주거는 어떻게 변했나요? 오늘날의 집과 20년 전의 집 사이의 가장 큰 차이는 무엇인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, housing in Korea? Let me think.' → 한 줄 요약(많이 변했다) → 차이 2개(집값, 스마트홈·편의 시설) → 내 경험(서울 작은 아파트 → 분당 15층 아파트) → 'So yeah, that's ~.'
___ has changed a lot over the years / The biggest difference is that ~ 로 변화를 정리하세요.
AL은 어릴 적 대전 마당 있는 집까지 넣어 세 시점을 비교하면 깊이가 생깁니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, housing in Korea? Let me think. Housing in Korea has changed a lot over the years. Twenty years ago, many apartments were old and small. These days, new apartments are bigger and have a lot of nice facilities, like gyms and parks. The biggest difference is that apartments are much more expensive now. When I started working, I lived in a small apartment in Seoul. Now I live in a nice apartment in Bundang with my family. So yeah, that's how housing has changed.
answers.IH: Oh, housing in Korea? Let me think. Housing in Korea has changed a lot over the years. First, apartments have become much more modern. Twenty years ago, most apartments were pretty basic. These days, new apartment complexes have gyms, playgrounds, cafes, and even smart home systems. I can turn on the heater with my phone before I get home. Parking is underground now, too. The biggest difference is that apartments are much more expensive now. Prices have gone up so much that it's really hard for young people to buy a home. For example, in my case, when I started working, I rented a tiny apartment in Seoul. It took me many years to save enough money to move to our current place in Bundang. So yeah, that's how housing has changed in Korea.
answers.AL: Oh, housing in Korea? That's a big question. Let me think. Housing in Korea has changed a lot over the years, and I've seen it with my own eyes. When I was a kid in Daejeon, my family lived in a house with a little yard, and most of my friends lived in houses too. But over the last 20 years, apartments have taken over almost everywhere. First of all, apartments have become way more modern. New complexes come with gyms, playgrounds, cafes, and smart home systems. I can turn on the heater with my phone on my way home, which would have sounded like science fiction back then. The biggest difference, though, is that apartments are much more expensive now. Prices have gone through the roof, so a lot of young people feel like owning a home is just a dream. For example, in my case, when I started working, I rented a tiny apartment in Seoul, and I had to save for years before we could move to our current place in Bundang. Honestly, I think we got lucky with the timing. When I think about my kids buying a home someday, it worries me a little. So yeah, that's how housing has changed in Korea.

questions.en: How has the movie industry changed over the years? How is the way people watch movies today different from the past, and what do you think about these changes?
questions.ko: 영화 산업은 수년간 어떻게 변했나요? 오늘날 사람들이 영화를 보는 방식은 과거와 어떻게 다르며, 이런 변화에 대해 어떻게 생각하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, movies? That's an interesting question.' → 과거(극장·비디오 대여점) → 현재(넷플릭스 같은 스트리밍) → 내 경험(금요일 가족 영화의 밤) → 내 생각(장단점) → 'So yeah, that's ~.'
These days, people tend to ~ / Compared to ~, ~ is much ~ 로 현재 경향과 비교를 말하세요.
마지막에 '그래도 큰 영화는 극장에서'처럼 균형 잡힌 의견을 한 줄 넣으면 IH 이상 점수에 좋습니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, movies? That's an interesting question. In the past, people usually went to the theater or rented videos to watch movies. These days, people tend to watch movies at home on streaming services like Netflix. Compared to the past, watching movies at home is much cheaper and easier. My family has a movie night every Friday at home. But I still go to the theater for big action movies. So yeah, that's how watching movies has changed.
answers.IH: Oh, movies? That's an interesting question. When I was in college, I usually went to the theater, or I rented videos from a small shop in my neighborhood. These days, people tend to watch movies at home on streaming services like Netflix. Compared to the past, watching movies at home is much cheaper and more convenient. You can watch anything, anytime, and you can pause it whenever you want. For example, my family has a movie night every Friday. We order chicken, sit on the sofa, and pick a movie together. With two kids, going to the theater every week would cost way too much. On the other hand, I think theaters are still special. For big sci-fi movies, the big screen and sound are just amazing. So yeah, that's what I think about these changes.
answers.AL: Oh, movies? That's an interesting question. The movie industry has changed so much since I was young. Back in my college days, if you wanted to see a movie, you went to the theater, or you rented a video from the little rental shop down the street and prayed it wasn't already taken. These days, people tend to watch movies at home on streaming services like Netflix, and some movies even skip theaters completely. Compared to the past, watching movies at home is much cheaper and more convenient. You can watch whatever you want, whenever you want, in your pajamas. For example, my family has a movie night every Friday. We order fried chicken, pile onto the sofa, and spend way too long arguing about what to watch. With two kids, going to the theater every week would cost a fortune, so streaming is a lifesaver for us. On the other hand, I think something has been lost. Theaters used to be a shared experience, and now everyone's glued to their own screen. So for big sci-fi movies, I still take my family to the theater, because nothing beats that huge screen and sound. All in all, it's a double-edged sword, but I think it's mostly a good change. So yeah, that's what I think about it.

questions.en: How has technology changed the way people listen to music? Compare how people listened to music in the past with how they do it now.
questions.ko: 기술은 사람들이 음악을 듣는 방식을 어떻게 바꿨나요? 과거와 현재 사람들이 음악을 듣는 방식을 비교해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, music and technology? Sure, let me think.' → 과거(카세트테이프, CD, MP3 플레이어) → 현재(스트리밍, 블루투스) → 내 경험(출퇴근 차에서 90년대 발라드, 아이들 덕에 K-pop) → 느낌 → 'So yeah, that's ~.'
I used to ~, but now I ~ 로 내 변화를 한 문장에 담고, The biggest difference is that ~ 로 정리하세요.
AL은 '음악이 너무 쉬워져서 앨범 하나를 아끼던 느낌이 사라졌다'처럼 감정적인 비교를 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Oh, music and technology? Sure, let me think. When I was a teenager in Daejeon, I listened to music on cassette tapes. Later, I bought CDs and used an MP3 player in college. I used to listen to CDs, but now I stream music in my car. I can listen to any song with just one tap. Thanks to my kids, I listen to K-pop too. The biggest difference is that music is so easy to find now. So yeah, that's how it has changed.
answers.IH: Oh, music and technology? Sure, let me think. When I was a teenager in Daejeon, I listened to music on a cassette player. I used to record songs from the radio, which took a lot of patience. In college, I bought CDs, and then I got my first MP3 player. I had to download every song and move it to the player. I used to listen to CDs, but now I stream music in my car. Every morning on my way to work, I just connect my phone and play my 90s ballad playlist. The biggest difference is that you can find any song in seconds, and it's really cheap. My kids even introduced me to K-pop, and now I know some of the songs too. So yeah, that's how technology has changed the way we listen to music.
answers.AL: Oh, music and technology? Sure, let me think. It's actually crazy how much it's changed in my lifetime. When I was a teenager in Daejeon, I listened to music on a cassette player, and I used to sit by the radio for hours waiting to record my favorite song, hitting the button at just the right moment. In college, I spent a big chunk of my allowance on CDs, and later I got my first MP3 player, which held only about a hundred songs. I used to listen to CDs, but now I stream music in my car. Every morning on my 20-minute drive, I just connect my phone and play my 90s ballad and rock playlist. The biggest difference is that you can find any song in the world in seconds, almost for free. Plus, streaming apps recommend new music based on what you like, which is pretty amazing. Thanks to my kids, I've even gotten into K-pop, and my daughter loves quizzing me on the members' names. On the other hand, I kind of miss the old days. Back then, every album felt precious, and I'd listen to it over and over. So yeah, that's how technology has changed the way we listen to music.

questions.en: What are some problems or concerns that people have about traveling these days? Why do you think these issues have come up?
questions.ko: 요즘 사람들이 여행에 대해 갖는 문제나 걱정에는 어떤 것들이 있나요? 왜 이런 문제들이 생겼다고 생각하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, problems with traveling? Let me think.' → 입장(걱정이 꽤 많다) → 문제·이유 2개(비용 상승, 관광지 혼잡) → 내 경험(작년 여름 오사카) → 결론 → 'So yeah, that's ~.'
Many people are concerned about ~ / I think this is because of ~ 로 문제와 원인을 연결하세요.
가족 넷이 가면 비용이 크다는 페르소나 디테일이 이유를 설득력 있게 만들어 줍니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, problems with traveling? Let me think. I think people have two big concerns these days. First, many people are concerned about rising travel costs. Flights and hotels are really expensive now. Second, popular places are too crowded. For example, last summer, my family went to Osaka. We waited almost two hours for one ride at Universal Studios. I think more people travel now because of social media. So yeah, that's what I think.
answers.IH: Oh, problems with traveling? Let me think. I think people have a few big concerns these days. First, many people are concerned about rising travel costs. Flights, hotels, and even food have gotten much more expensive. For a family of four like mine, one overseas trip costs a lot of money. Second, popular places are getting way too crowded. For example, last summer, my family went to Osaka. It was a great trip, but there were tourists everywhere. At Universal Studios, we waited almost two hours for one ride, and my kids got really tired. I think these issues came up because traveling became so popular after the pandemic. Also, people see beautiful photos on social media, and everyone wants to go to the same places. So yeah, that's what I think about it.
answers.AL: Oh, problems with traveling these days? That's a big question. Let me think. I believe that traveling has become a lot more stressful for two main reasons. First, many people are concerned about rising travel costs. Flights, hotels, and even a simple lunch cost way more than they did a few years ago. For a family of four like mine, an overseas trip is a serious investment, so we have to plan months ahead. Second, popular places are getting overcrowded. For example, last summer, my family went to Osaka. Don't get me wrong, it was an amazing trip, but there were tourists literally everywhere. At Universal Studios, we waited almost two hours for one ride, and by the afternoon, my daughter was so exhausted that I had to carry her on my back. I think these issues came up because everyone started traveling at once after the pandemic, so demand went through the roof. On top of that, social media makes everyone want to visit the exact same photo spots. Some local people even complain that tourists are ruining their neighborhoods. All things considered, I think travel is still worth it, but we need to travel smarter, like going in the off-season. So yeah, that's what I think about it.

questions.en: Some people prefer working from home, while others prefer working at the office. What are the advantages and disadvantages of each? Which do you prefer, and why?
questions.ko: 어떤 사람들은 재택근무를, 어떤 사람들은 사무실 근무를 선호합니다. 각각의 장단점은 무엇인가요? 당신은 어느 쪽을 선호하며, 그 이유는 무엇인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, working from home? I have a lot to say about that.' → 입장(둘을 섞은 방식이 최고) → 이유 2개(재택: 출퇴근 없음·집중 / 사무실: 소통·멘토링) → 내 경험(금요일 재택, 팀 리드) → 결론 → 'So yeah, that's ~.'
I believe that ~ for two reasons → First / Second → All things considered, I think ~ 순서를 그대로 쓰세요.
20년 전엔 재택이 상상도 못 할 일이었다는 비교를 한 줄 넣으면 AL다운 답이 됩니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, working from home? Sure, let me think. I work from home on Fridays, so I know both sides. Working from home is comfortable, and I don't have to drive to work. But at the office, it's easier to talk with my team. I'm a team leader, so I need to meet my team members a lot. I believe that a mix of home and office work is best for two reasons. It's flexible, and it keeps the team close. So yeah, that's what I think.
answers.IH: Oh, working from home? Sure, I have a lot to say about that. I work from home on Fridays, so I know both sides pretty well. Working from home has some big advantages. I don't have to commute, and it's quiet, so I can focus on difficult work. I can also have lunch with my kids sometimes. But it has disadvantages too. It's hard to stop working because my laptop is always right there. Working at the office is better for teamwork. As a team leader, I need to help new developers, and that's much easier face to face. I believe that a mix of home and office work is best for two reasons. First, people get some flexibility. Second, the team still stays connected. So yeah, that's what I think about it.
answers.AL: Oh, working from home? Sure, I have a lot to say about that. When I started my career 20 years ago, working from home was unthinkable, but now I do it every Friday, so I've seen both sides. I believe that a mix of home and office work is best for two reasons. First, working from home saves a ton of time and energy. I don't have to sit in traffic, and it's quiet, so I can really focus on tricky problems without people tapping me on the shoulder every five minutes. I can even have lunch with my kids when they get home early. But the downside is that the line between work and home gets blurry, and I sometimes catch myself checking messages at ten at night. Second, the office is much better for teamwork and mentoring. As a team leader with ten people, I've noticed that new developers learn way faster when they can just turn around and ask a question. My coworker Minho and I solve problems in five minutes at the whiteboard that would take an hour over chat. All things considered, I think the best option is somewhere in the middle, a few days at the office and a day or two at home. So yeah, that's what I think about it.

questions.en: Compare living in a big city with living in a small town. Which do you think is better for young people, and why?
questions.ko: 대도시에서 사는 것과 작은 마을에서 사는 것을 비교해 주세요. 젊은 사람들에게는 어느 쪽이 더 낫다고 생각하며, 그 이유는 무엇인가요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 'Oh, big city or small town? Let me think.' → 비교(도시: 일자리·편의 / 작은 동네: 조용함·여유) → 입장(젊은 사람에겐 대도시) → 이유 2개 → 내 경험(대전의 조용한 동네에서 자람 → 서울에서 신입 시절) → 결론 → 'So yeah, that's ~.'
I believe that ~ for two reasons / All things considered, I think ~ 로 의견을 분명하게 정리하세요.
지금은 분당처럼 도시 근처 조용한 동네를 선택했다는 '인생 단계에 따라 다르다' 결론을 넣으면 균형이 잡힙니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, big city or small town? Let me think. Big cities have more jobs, more things to do, and better transportation. Small towns are quiet, and life is slower and cheaper. I grew up in a quiet neighborhood in Daejeon, and then I started my career in Seoul. I believe that big cities are better for young people for two reasons. There are more jobs, and you can meet a lot of people. So yeah, that's what I think.
answers.IH: Oh, big city or small town? Let me think. Both have good points. Big cities have a lot of jobs, great restaurants, and convenient public transportation. But they're crowded, noisy, and expensive. Small towns are quiet and peaceful, and houses are cheaper, but there aren't many jobs. I believe that big cities are better for young people for two reasons. First, there are many more job opportunities. Second, you can meet all kinds of people and learn new things. For example, in my case, I grew up in a quiet neighborhood in Daejeon. After college, I moved to Seoul for my first job, and I learned so much there. Now that I have a family, I prefer a calmer place like Bundang. All things considered, I think a big city is better for young people. So yeah, that's my opinion.
answers.AL: Oh, big city or small town? That's a tough one. Let me think. Honestly, both have their pros and cons. Big cities have tons of jobs, great restaurants, and super convenient public transportation, but they can be crowded, noisy, and ridiculously expensive. Small towns, on the other hand, are quiet and peaceful, and housing is way cheaper, but there just aren't many job opportunities, especially in tech. I believe that big cities are better for young people for two reasons. First, that's where the opportunities are. Most big companies and startups are in or near Seoul, so it's much easier to start a career there. Second, when you're young, it's important to meet all kinds of people and try new things. For example, in my case, I grew up in a quiet neighborhood in Daejeon, where everybody knew each other. After college, I moved to Seoul for my first job, and those years in the city really shaped who I am today. That said, things change as you get older. Now that I have two kids, I prefer a calmer place like Bundang, with parks and walking trails nearby. All things considered, I think a big city is better for young people, and a quieter place is better for families. So yeah, that's what I think about it.

pronunciation.tip: '나'에 강세. '테크놀로지'처럼 모든 음절을 똑같이 읽지 않기
'비'에 강세, v는 윗니로 아랫입술을 살짝 물고

patterns.en: Housing in Korea has changed a lot over the years.
The biggest difference is that apartments are much more expensive now.
patterns.ko: 가장 큰 차이는 요즘 아파트가 훨씬 비싸졌다는 거예요.

patterns.en: These days, people tend to watch movies at home on streaming services like Netflix.
patterns.ko: 요즘 사람들은 넷플릭스 같은 스트리밍 서비스로 집에서 영화를 보는 경향이 있어요.

patterns.en: Compared to the past, watching movies at home is much cheaper and more convenient.
patterns.ko: 예전에 비해 집에서 영화를 보는 게 훨씬 싸고 편리해요.

patterns.en: I used to listen to CDs, but now I stream music in my car.
patterns.ko: 예전엔 CD로 음악을 들었는데, 지금은 차에서 스트리밍으로 들어요.

patterns.en: Many people are concerned about rising travel costs.
patterns.ko: 많은 사람들이 오르는 여행 경비를 걱정해요.

patterns.en: I believe that a mix of home and office work is best for two reasons.
patterns.ko: 저는 두 가지 이유로 재택과 사무실 근무를 섞는 게 가장 좋다고 생각해요.

patterns.en: All things considered, I think a big city is better for young people.
patterns.ko: 모든 걸 고려하면, 젊은 사람들에게는 대도시가 더 낫다고 생각해요.
